investigator.method: Bounded Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC triage-refinement: one unauthenticated GET to the candidate's official_website (via curl, descriptive User-Agent, redirects followed, 25s timeout, no retries), plus one additional unauthenticated GET to the candidate's given official_programme_url under the same bounds. No browser, authentication, CAPTCHA-bypass, or state-changing request was used.

probe_history.reason: Single unauthenticated GET to the candidate's official_website, plus a single additional GET to the given official_programme_url (https://ica.art/2026-07?calendar), to establish identity and the balance of current programme categories.

venue_reference: Institute of Contemporary Arts -- second London tranche triage-refinement candidate (osm-node-5015865539)

identity.notes: The retrieved page's own <title> ('ICA | Institute of Contemporary Arts') and meta description ('The Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA) is London's leading space for contemporary culture...') identify this as the ICA's own official site.

site_classification.platform: Server-rendered calendar/listing site with a dated day-by-day programme (also probed at the given official_programme_url, https://ica.art/2026-07?calendar, which server-rendered the July 2026 daily programme for 1 July 2026).

reasons: Real retrieved evidence shows the ICA's current programme is genuinely mixed across Exhibitions, Films, Talks & Events, and Live (music/performance) -- with Film and visual-arts content outnumbering music items on both the homepage listing and the sampled daily-programme page.

Music events are real and dated (e.g. 'CTM x ICA 2026', 24-25 September 2026) but form only a minority category, requiring deeper per-category filtering before any acquisition path targeting music specifically could be built.

evidence.description: Retained, bounded, literal excerpt(s) of the actual HTTP response body/bodies from the candidate's official_website and the given official_programme_url -- each excerpt is a contiguous, unedited substring of the real retrieved HTML, capped well under 4KB per item; the surrounding full response was not retained in full (bounded capture, not a full-page dump).
evidence.method: curl GET; descriptive User-Agent; unauthenticated; redirects followed; 25-second timeout; single request per URL; no retry; no authentication, CAPTCHA-bypass, or state-changing request
